title: ERIS: Enhancing the Privacy–Utility–Scalability Trade-Off in Federated Learning via Federated Shard Aggregation
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: A client update is compressed and split into shards, each aggregated by a different client-side aggregator, then returned to all clients.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; left client steps top-down, right client-aggregator graphs
description: Two boxed panels. The left panel, "Client Computation at Round t", is a vertical flow of three stages joined by thick down arrows. A gradient is drawn as a gray grid and a neural-net icon. It passes through a shaded lavender "Distributed Shifted Compression" block, where the grid is partly hatched. It then reaches "FSA Model Partitioning", where the grid is split into blue and green shards. Math labels sit beside the arrows. The right panel, "FSA Distributed Model Aggregation at Round t", shows clients C1, C2, C3, Ck and Ck-1 as circles. Blue and green arrows carry small colored network icons, first from clients to the two aggregators (double-ringed C2 and Ck-1), then back to all clients. A central "Aggregation" arrow has the update equations beneath it. Blue and green coding links the shards across the panels.
caption: Illustration of eris at training round $t$ for two aggregators ($A\!=\!2$). Left: each client optionally applies \compline{DSC} and then performs FSA partitioning, generating shards \( v^t_{k,(a)} \) sent to aggregators \( C_2 \) and \( C_{k-1} \). Right: each aggregator collects and aggregates the corresponding shards across clients to produce partial updated models \( x^{t+1}_{(a)} \), which are sent back to the clients.
abstract: Scaling Federated Learning (FL) to billion-parameter models forces a challenging trade-off between privacy, scalability, and model utility. Existing solutions often tackle these challenges in isolation, sacrificing accuracy, relying on costly cryptographic tools, or introducing communication and optimization inefficiencies that affect convergence. We introduce ERIS, an FL framework centered on Federated Shard Aggregation (FSA), a novel mechanism that partitions each client update into non-overlapping shards whose aggregation is distributed across multiple client-side aggregators. FSA removes the central aggregation bottleneck, limits the information visible to any single observer, and preserves the centralized FL update after reassembly. ERIS can further readily integrate Distributed Shifted Compression (DSC) to reduce transmitted payloads and exposed coordinates. We prove that ERIS preserves convergence under standard assumptions and bounds mutual information leakage by the observable fraction of each update, decreasing with the number of client-side aggregators, and with the compression level when DSC is enabled. Experiments across image and text tasks, including large language models, show that ERIS achieves FedAvg-level utility while substantially reducing communication bottlenecks and improving robustness to membership inference and reconstruction attacks, without relying on heavy cryptography or utility-degrading perturbations.
